findings.note: The staging-directory containment guard is wired into the PUBLISH path only, not the RECOVERY path, and the recovery path performs a recursive delete. Every converged outcome in _recover_journal (SAFE completion, SAFE abandonment, MIX) ends in _discard_batch, which unlinks the journal then rmtree's the batch dir. If specs/<feature>/.resolver-staging is a SYMLINK, Path.glob traverses it and os.path.islink(batch_dir) is False for the real directory behind it, so rmtree does not refuse: the recursively deleted directory is OUTSIDE specs/<feature>/. Both ingredients are ordinary committed files on a malicious branch - the threat model _recover_journal's own TRUST BOUNDARY comment already accepts. The planted journal needs no escaping target at all: a single entry naming an in-set, currently-absent target (pre_hash ABSENT) classifies as all-PRE / SAFE abandonment and reaches _discard_batch directly, so the round-1 allowlist and round-2 _target_escapes_via_symlink check are never consulted. Destructive write outside the fixed named set (requirements.md Security Boundaries bullet 1), strictly worse than round 1's single-file unlink, and not covered by either recorded disposition.

findings.ref: T-007.md Specification Differences item 2; resolve-project-context.py main() step-0.5 handler -> _block -> _write_evidence
findings.note: The report states that on a publication-journal-recovery Block, design.md's 'live state exactly as found' is 'honoured for the journal's own targets'. Not strictly true: _block publishes resolver-evidence.yaml, itself one of the four allowlisted targets a retained journal may list, moving it off both its recorded PRE and POST hash and potentially converting an operator-fixable batch into one that can no longer be converged. The AC-012-grounded decision to write Evidence here is defensible and disclosed; the claim about the journal's own targets being untouched is the part that overstates.

findings.ref: resolve-project-context.py _publish_bundle staging containment guard inside the try/except OSError block
findings.note: os.path.commonpath raises ValueError, not OSError, when its arguments share no common prefix in the drive sense (Windows cross-drive junction/subst). The surrounding handler catches OSError only, so that case would escape main() as an uncaught traceback rather than the canonical artifact-publication-failed line REQ-002/AC-014 require, and would bypass _rollback_transaction. Unreachable on POSIX; noted as a robustness/diagnostic-format gap.

findings.ref: Assessment of the two recorded dispositions (non-blocking, recorded for the gate)
findings.note: Both dispositions are honestly recorded and correctly reasoned from the bundle's own frozen text; neither is re-raised. (a) The doubly-degraded rollback corner is a genuine three-clause collision, all three clauses present verbatim, both repair options requiring a fourth journal operation the frozen contract does not define; the owner's 2026-08-27 option-(a) selection is recorded in the report and in situ. (b) The PRE-image provenance finding is correctly out of scope: security-spec.md's Cryptographic Failures row (no signing key, no HMAC, no credential) and Authorization row (no live wiring yet) are present as cited, and authenticating on-disk provenance against an adversary with disk write access does require a secret the frozen spec deliberately excludes. One qualification: that disposition's fourth ground asserts round 1 closed writes OUTSIDE the fixed named set as an absolute invariant; the Critical above shows that invariant is not yet fully delivered on the recovery path, so the line the disposition leans on is not yet actually drawn. This qualifies the framing without changing the conclusion. Separately, the transaction sequence itself is faithful and non-vacuously proven within its own wired scope.
